subject: Electrical Machines
question: An ideal single-phase transformer has 500 turns on the primary and 100 turns on the secondary. With 220 V (RMS) applied to the primary, what is the no-load secondary voltage?
solution: For an ideal transformer the voltage ratio equals the turns ratio: V2/V1 = N2/N1. So V2 = 220 x 100/500 = 44 V. The secondary current would be 5 times the primary current, but the voltage steps down by the same factor.
author: Rajon Das
